title: Legislative districts of Ilocos Sur

{{Short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}} {{Politics of the Philippines}}[[File:Legislative_Districts_of_Ilocos_Sur.png|border|400x400px]] The '''legislative districts of Ilocos Sur''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Ilocos Sur]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#1st District|first]] and [[#2nd District|second]] congressional districts. [[Abra (province)|Abra]] last formed part of the province's representation in 1917. The [[#1st District|first district of Ilocos Sur]] is among the original representative districts from 1907 which has never changed in territorial coverage, along with [[Legislative districts of Albay#1st District|Albay's first]], [[Legislative districts of Ilocos Norte#1st District|Ilocos Norte's first]] and [[Legislative districts of Ilocos Norte#2nd District|second]], and [[Legislative districts of Iloilo#1st District|Iloilo's first]] districts. == History == Ilocos Sur, which at the time included the sub-province of [[Abra (province)|Abra]], was initially divided in 1907 into three [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|representative districts]]. [[Abra (province)|Abra]] was last represented as part of the province's now-defunct [[#3rd District (defunct)|third district]] in 1917, after its re-establishment as a regular province on March 10, 1917, by virtue of Act No. 2683 warranted its [[Legislative district of Abra|separate representation]], thereby reducing Ilocos Sur to two districts.{{cite journal|author=Philippine Legislature|title=Public Laws Enacted by the Philippine Legislature, Acts No. 2657 to 2710|journal=Public Resolutions, Etc |series=Laws, etc |date=1917|publisher=Bureau of Printing Office|page=168|url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.35112103552156;view=1up;seq=202|access-date=February 5, 2017}} When the Philippine Commission detached [[Tagudin]] from [[Ilocos Sur]] and made it the capital of the sub-province of [[Amburayan]] in [[Mountain Province]] on May 15, 1907, by virtue of Act No. 1646, the town's residents were still allowed to vote as part of the Ilocos Sur's [[#1907–1916|second district]].{{cite book|author=United States Philippine Commission|title=Acts of the Philippine Commission, nos. 1539–1800, inclusive|date=1907|publisher=U.S. Government Printing Office|pages=153–155|url=https://archive.org/stream/actsphilippinec02unkngoog#page/n182/mode/2up|access-date=February 2, 2017|format=Book digitized by [[Google]] from the library of [[Harvard University]] and uploaded to the Internet Archive on June 21, 2009}} This arrangement was terminated on August 10, 1916, under Act No. 2657 (the Administrative Code of the Philippine Islands), which removed the town from the second district.{{cite book|author=Philippine Legislature|title=Administrative Code of the Philippine Islands (Act No. 2657)|date=1916|publisher=U.S. Government Printing Office|page=62|url=https://archive.org/stream/lawsthirdphilip00philgoog#page/n64/mode/2up|access-date=February 2, 2017|format=Book digitized by [[Google]] from the library of [[Harvard University]] and uploaded to the Internet Archive on September 29, 2008}} The enactment of Act No. 2877 in 1920 reorganized northwestern Luzon, by abolishing the sub-province of [[Amburayan]] in the undivided [[Mountain Province]] and annexing several of its municipal entities—[[Alilem]], [[Sigay, Ilocos Sur|Sigay]], [[Sugpon]], [[Suyo, Ilocos Sur|Suyo]] and its capital [[Tagudin]]—to Ilocos Sur. The Lepanto sub-province townships of [[Quirino, Ilocos Sur|Angaki]], [[Gregorio del Pilar, Ilocos Sur|Concepcion]], [[San Emilio, Ilocos Sur|San Emilio]] and its capital [[Cervantes, Ilocos Sur|Cervantes]] were also placed under the jurisdiction of Ilocos Sur. However residents of these areas remained represented by the Mountain Province's [[Legislative district of Mountain Province#1917–1935|appointed assembly members]] until they were finally extended the right to vote in assembly district elections in 1935, after the passage of Act No. 4203 placed them in the [[#2nd District|second district]] of Ilocos Sur.{{cite journal|author=Philippine Legislature|title=Public Laws Enacted by the Philippine Legislature, Acts No. 4203 to 4275|journal=Public Resolutions, Etc |series=Laws, etc |date=1937|publisher=Bureau of Printing Office|page=4|url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.35112102880830;view=1up;seq=132|access-date=February 2, 2017}} Ilocos Sur was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region I]] from 1978 to 1984, and elected [[#At-Large (defunct)|two representatives]] to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. The province retained its [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|two congressional districts]] under the new Constitution{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=June 13, 2016}} which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, and elected members to the restored House of Representatives starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. == Current districts and representatives == Ilocos Sur's current congressional delegation is composed of two members. {{Color box|{{party color|Nationalist People's Coalition}}|border=darkgray}} [[Nationalist People's Coalition|NPC]] (2) {| class="wikitable sortable" style="margin: 1em auto; font-size:100%; line-height:20px; text-align:center" |+Legislative districts and representatives of [[Ilocos Sur]] ! rowspan="2" |District ! colspan="3" |Current Representative ! rowspan="2" |Party ! rowspan="2" |Constituent [[Local government in the Philippines|LGUs]] ! rowspan="2" |Population (2020){{PH census|2020|01}} ! rowspan="2" |Area{{Cite web |title=List of Provinces |url=http://www.nscb.gov.ph/activestats/psgc/listprov.asp |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160419000512/http://www.nscb.gov.ph/activestats/psgc/listprov.asp |archive-date=April 19, 2016 |access-date=August 2, 2022 |website=PSGC Interactive |publisher=National Statistical Coordination Board}} ! rowspan="2" |Map |- ! colspan="2" |Image !Name |- ![[Ilocos Sur's 1st congressional district|1st]] | style="background:{{party color|Nationalist People's Coalition}};" | | [[File:Rep.
